Hmm OK — but WAIT, this changes the picture entirely! If apply_quakeworld_prefs crashes at init... but ARVO/OSS-Fuzz ran fuzzshark successfully for other inputs — the harness must not crash at startup. Unless... the crash at startup IS what happens with quakeworld target?? No — OSS-Fuzz would never find a proper crash; every run would crash.

So maybe I'm wrong about the NULL. Let me check prefs_find_preference behavior — maybe it g_asserts... Let me read lines 1030-1080 of prefs.c.

Actually, hold on — alternative: maybe the UDP module has a "udp.port" pref? No, prefs_find_module("quakeworld") gives quakeworld module.

Hmm, actually, wait — I should check prefs.c's prefs_find_preference:

```c
pref_t *prefs_find_preference(module_t *module, const char *name)
{
    ...
    for each pref in module->prefs... compare names; if module has submodules? 
}
```

If not found returns NULL. So apply_quakeworld_prefs → NULL deref. Unless this version of prefs.c has special handling. Let me read it.

Hmm, but ALSO — hmm, wait. Actually, maybe the apply callback is never invoked if the module has NO prefs changed? prefs_apply_all iterates all modules and calls apply callbacks... let me check: prefs_apply_all → walk_modules → module->apply_cb ... For every module with apply_cb != NULL? Let me check.

Actually, let me now also reconsider the whole approach: maybe THIS is the vulnerability! "overflow can occur while writing to a buffer" — hmm, no, NULL deref is not an overflow.

Hmm wait, actually — hmm, let me reconsider. Maybe apply_quakeworld_prefs is fine because prefs_get_uint_value in THIS version takes (module, name) and prefs_find_preference handles NULL module... still NULL.

OK, I need to stop speculating and check prefs.c prefs_apply_all and prefs_find_preference code paths.
